items.title: Introduce World as the turn-based step owner

brief.goal: The game is turn-based: World::step(Action) is the only way time moves, the frontend holds no simulation state, and the world waits for the player.
units: core: add src/core/include/peo/core/action.hpp: enum class ActionKind { Step, Wait }; struct Action { ActionKind kind; Vec2i dir; static Action step(Vec2i); static Action wait(); }.

core: add src/core/include/peo/core/world.hpp: struct WorldParams { int initial_dead = 40; float player_scent = 1.0F; ScentParams scent; }; class World { public: World(Seed, WorldParams = {}); void load_stage(uint32_t); void step(Action); const Stage& stage() const; const ScentField& scent() const; const std::vector<Dead>& horde() const; Vec2i player() const; Tick turn() const; uint32_t stage_index() const; }. No clock, no thread, no SDL.

core: implement src/core/src/world.cpp by moving load_stage/try_move/simulate out of main.cpp. step(): apply action (a Step into a wall becomes a Wait, still consumes the turn), deposit scent at player cell, scent.step(&blocked), step_horde, ++turn; reaching the exit loads the next stage at the end of the turn. Add both files to src/core/CMakeLists.txt.

test: tests/core/test_world.cpp — 'same seed same world after 100 turns' (two Worlds fed the same actions: equal player, horde, scent.total()), 'step into wall consumes the turn but does not move', 'wait advances the turn and the dead approach', 'reaching exit advances stage_index'. Register in tests/CMakeLists.txt; suite stays under 500 ms.

app: main.cpp keeps SDL setup, key mapping, draw(). App holds a World and a 'dirty' flag; a key press calls world.step(Action) exactly once; nothing advances on a timer. Remove kTickMs, last_tick_ms and the pause toggle (a turn-based game has no pause). Keep Shift+S scent view and N next stage.
docs: in docs/architecture.md 'Planned seams', mark World as built and note the file names.
acceptance: src/app/main.cpp contains no ScentField, Rng, Dead or Stage manipulation; only World calls, input mapping and drawing
the world does not change while the player is idle for 10 seconds
one key press moves the player one cell and the Dead one step at most
the four new world tests pass; whole suite under 500 ms
manual: Run ./build/dev/bin/peo 7. Do nothing for 10 s: nothing on screen may change.
Press right 20 times: @ moves one cell per press; the d glyphs close in one cell per press.
Hold a movement key: movement must feel immediate with no queued lag after release (report the OS key-repeat feel).
Press . or space (wait): the Dead advance one step while @ stays.
Walk into > : stage counter increments and the map changes.
out_of_scope: blood or other scent layers — PEO-003
corpse descriptors for individual Dead — later item

notes.text: briefed; Architect will write test_world.cpp expectations on request, Builder may write them per unit 3

items.title: Compute the next turn while waiting for input

brief.goal: Between turns the world speculates the next turn assuming Wait; on input, commit() patches only the player's neighbourhood and produces state bit-identical to step().
units: core: make ScentField::step linear-then-clamp explicitly: split into step_linear(blocked) and clamp_floor(); step() calls both. Add ScentField::patch_deposit(Vec2i at, float amount): applies diffuse(δ) for a single deposit to the 5 affected cells (respecting walls exactly as step_linear does), assuming the field is already post-step_linear. Test: for random fields and deposits, step_linear on (field+δ) equals step_linear(field) then patch_deposit(δ), exactly (use == not Approx; choose operation order so this holds).

core: add struct Speculation { ScentField scent; std::vector<Dead> horde; Tick turn; } and World::speculate() const -> Speculation: the full turn assuming Action::wait() and no player deposit. Pure; no member mutation.

core: add World::commit(Speculation&&, Action): apply the action, patch_deposit at the player's cell, clamp_floor, then re-run the move decision only for Dead within 2 cells of the player's new cell (reset them from the pre-turn positions kept in the Speculation), resolve contact, adopt the result. Add static bool World::equivalent(const World&, const World&) for tests.

test: golden test in tests/core/test_world.cpp: for 200 random (seed, action sequence) pairs, run A: step(action) each turn, B: commit(speculate(), action) each turn; assert equivalent() after every turn. Include steps into walls and stage transitions.

test: perf sanity (headless-release): at 200x120 with 5000 Dead, report microseconds for speculate() and commit() via doctest -d; commit must be under 1 ms on the Builder's machine (record the number).

app: main.cpp spawns one std::jthread that, whenever the world is idle and no speculation exists, computes world.speculate() into a buffer; the input handler calls commit() if a fresh speculation exists, else step(). The renderer reads only the committed World. Add an on-screen HUD flag 'spec:hit/miss' for the manual test.
docs: architecture.md 'Computing while waiting' gets the final function names and the measured numbers.
acceptance: golden test passes for 200 random sequences: commit(speculate()) is bit-identical to step()
commit() under 1 ms and speculate() under 16 ms at 200x120 with 5000 Dead on the Builder's machine (release)
core spawns no threads; the only thread lives in src/app/main.cpp
in game, HUD shows spec:hit on nearly every turn when playing at human speed
manual: Run the release build with seed 7. Play 100 turns at normal speed: HUD should read spec:hit almost always; report the miss count.
Mash a movement key as fast as possible for 5 s: no crash, no visual glitch, misses allowed; report feel.
Compare a 50-turn walk in debug vs release with the same key sequence: the Dead must end in the same cells (determinism across builds).
out_of_scope: multi-turn lookahead beyond one Wait turn

items.title: Weighted-draw movement for the Dead with aggregates and company pull

brief.goal: step_horde becomes the round-3 weighted draw (scent, aggregate, company, repellent, footing terms) and the swarm-accumulation and fan-out scenarios pass headlessly.

notes.text: D-007 (see decisions.md) fixes the shape of the draw: weight a candidate cell by pow(scent, k) with a tunable exponent k slightly above 1, never exp(k*scent) — at the 0-500 scale from PEO-026 exp saturates immediately. A power law keys off the ratio between neighbouring cells, so one k stays decisive next to the player and becomes a gentle drift far away, which is the horde-drift behaviour the user asked for. Fold this into the brief when PEO-009 is planned.

items.title: The Dead do not converge within 3 s: scent spreads ~8 cells in 20 s, so distant Dead never move

brief.goal: The Dead converge from across the map: the scent field carries a usable gradient to the map edges on a 0-500 scale, so none of the Dead is ever frozen on a flat zero field.
units: core: raise the deposit scale. kPlayerScent already exists at src/app/main.cpp:26 as 1.0F — change it to 500.0F and move it into core beside ScentParams so tests and any future depositor share one constant. Note the field step is linear, so deposit magnitude and floor are interchangeable (500.0F at floor 1e-6 is the same field shape as 1.0F at 2e-9); the 500 scale is chosen for the integer draw weights PEO-009 needs, and buys a constant ~28 cells of reach on top of the floor change.

core: retune the ScentParams defaults in scent.hpp. Start from diffusion 0.8, decay 0.01, floor 1e-6 — these were arrived at independently on branch claude/fervent-curie-iqonhg from the same root cause, and give sqrt((0.8/4)/0.01) = 4.47 cells per e-fold, about 90 cells of steady-state reach at a 500.0F deposit on an 80x45 map. Keep diffusion under 1.0 (the explicit scheme goes unstable at the limit; 0.8 means out = 0.8*here in the interior). Record the values you settle on in the report.

test: tests/core/test_scent.cpp — add 'the scent front crosses the map': open 80x45, deposit kPlayerScent at (8,22) every step for 200 steps, then CHECK sample({70,22}) > 0.0F and CHECK values strictly decrease along y=22 from x=9 to x=70. Do not stop at a bare '> 0.0F' check against a 1e-6 floor: that pins the exponential tail crossing zero, not a usable scent level, so the strict-decrease assertion is the one that matters.

test: tests/core/test_dead.cpp — add 'distant Dead close in': same field, one of the Dead starting at (60,22) must close at least 25 cells over 200 calls to step_horde. This is the real regression test for this bug — it asserts behaviour, not field values.

app: the scent view's bands are tuned for a 0..1 field and will render as one solid block at the new scale. Make the bands relative to the field maximum or log-spaced so the view survives retuning. Overlaps PEO-024 (new glyph for the strongest band): land the second of the two on top of the first.
docs: one line in docs/design/scent-mobs.md recording the 0-500 deposit scale and that reach goes as sqrt((diffusion/4)/decay) * ln(peak/floor).
acceptance: on an open map the field is strictly positive and strictly decreasing out to at least 60 cells from the player: no flat zero region inside the map
in game (peo 7): standing still, the Dead close in from across the map, not only from within ~8 cells

both new tests pass and the whole suite stays under 500 ms — size the new cases deliberately: the briefed scent-reach case (200 steps over 80x45) is more cell-updates than the heaviest case in the suite today, so use the smallest field and step count that still demonstrates the reach
ScentField::step stays linear: no value-dependent decay and no pow/exp inside step. The floor flush remains the only nonlinearity, so PEO-007's step_linear + clamp_floor split survives.
no magic numbers: the deposit and every retuned default is a named constant or a ScentParams field
the thousand-dead case is no slower than the PEO-027 baseline above
manual: peo 7: stand still 30 s. The Dead should close in from the far side of the map, not only from nearby. Report roughly how many turns before a distant one first moves.
Shift+S: the scent view must still show a readable gradient rather than one solid block. Describe what it looks like.
Walk a long loop, then stand still: report whether the Dead track your current position or trail toward where you have been. This tells us whether decay needs raising.

headless-release: re-run the thousand-dead case and report the number. The old 0.000735 s figure is void — it was ~99% scent diffusion, and PEO-027 shortened that warm-up. The current baseline is 0.000261 s.
out_of_scope: the weighted random draw and the pow(scent, k) draw exponent — that is PEO-009, which D-007 also covers
making the field integer or fixed-point: D-007 keeps storage float deliberately, since quantising cells would recreate the plateau that froze the Dead

notes.text: Raised D-007 (scent reach / convergence pacing). Blocked on the pacing answer: the front-radius test in this brief can only pin a number once the target reach is chosen. Technical instrumentation is ready to write behind the decision.

D-007 answered and recorded in decisions.md; briefed. Root cause identified from the code: the ~8-cell reach is the floor flush in scent.cpp (v < floor -> 0.0F, floor 0.001F against a 1.0F deposit); past it the field is exactly zero, strongest_neighbour requires v > best strictly, so distant Dead never move. Fix is dynamic range, not diffusion rate.

Brief corrected: kPlayerScent already exists at src/app/main.cpp:26 as 1.0F, so the unit raises it rather than introducing it. Starting tuning values (diffusion 0.8, decay 0.01, floor 1e-6) are carried over from branch claude/fervent-curie-iqonhg, which reached the same numbers independently; that branch's pinning test asserted only sample > 0.0F against a 1e-6 floor, which passes on the tail crossing rather than a usable scent level, so the tests here assert a strictly decreasing gradient and actual Dead convergence instead.
